page: Amazon Web Services t3.2xlarge is an x86_64 general-purpose instance featuring burstable CPU performance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The virtual machine provides 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores and 8 threads via an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. It includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a 35 MB shared L3 cache, with instruction support for AVX, AVX-512F, AES, and FMA. Memory capacity totals 32.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance comes with no bundled local storage, relying on external network volumes, contains no hardware GPU accelerators, and delivers a baseline network throughput of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark results highlight the behavioral characteristics of the burstable Intel platform. In compute evaluations, multi-core throughput lands in average tiers with a PassMark CPU score of 7,482.86 and a multi-core stress-ng metric of 6,740.18. Conversely, single-threaded metrics show limitations, registering a weak stress-ng score of 1,265.99 and a Geekbench single-core score of 811.0. Memory performance reflects average large-block write speeds of 27.42 GB/sec alongside weaker uncached read bandwidth at 34.0 GB/sec. Data processing tests show slower single- and multi-threaded compression metrics, while in-memory operations demonstrate solid capability with Redis SET throughput reaching 6.32 million operations per second.

From an architectural standpoint, the t3.2xlarge offers qualitative resource density for workloads that experience fluctuating demand rather than sustained high CPU load. The lack of integrated local disks necessitates remote block storage, and the burstable processor model imposes constraints under continuous computation once CPU credits deplete. Consequently, the instance is well suited for medium-traffic web servers, development environments, staging systems, build and integration nodes, and intermediate caching layers that benefit from 32 GB of memory without requiring continuous maximum CPU utilization.
description: Amazon Web Services t3.2xlarge is a burstable general-purpose virtual machine built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor. Operating on the x86_64 architecture at 2.5 GHz, the configuration supplies 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores, paired with 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory at a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The server lacks onboard local storage and dedicated GPU acceleration, utilizing remote storage and delivering a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. Empirical benchmark testing reflects average multi-core processing capability alongside weaker single-threaded compute and compression metrics, balanced by steady memory write speeds and solid in-memory throughput of 6.32 million Redis SET operations per second. Due to its burstable allocation profile and moderate network baseline, the instance provides cost-effective resource density for variable workloads such as staging environments, CI/CD runners, intermediate cache layers, and moderate-throughput application backends.
